EUR.catalyst: The euro is trading near the 1.1215 level against the dollar, remaining capped below its 20-day, 50-day, and 200-day moving averages amid a broader weekly underperformance across the G10 complex. While headline Eurozone inflation for September printed above expectations at 3.8% alongside an 18.8% annual jump in energy costs, dovish pushback from European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde regarding unwarranted market moves prompted traders to reduce the probability of an October rate hike from roughly 75% to 28%. Bilateral capital flows are also contending with real policy rate divergence against Scandinavian peers like the Swedish krona, leaving the shared currency vulnerable pending fresh economic projections.

AUD.catalyst: The Australian dollar is displaying strong G10 outperformance, advancing 0.29% on the session and 0.73% over the week, even as it trades around 0.6961 against the dollar below its major moving averages. Markets are monitoring key indicators over the upcoming trading week, focusing specifically on household spending, wage growth, and labor market figures to gauge whether the RBA's restrictive stance will endure into early 2027.
